prompt.context: The new CEO of HealthCorp, a not-for-profit health insurer, has recently engaged you to help her solve a budding problem. Over the last 3 years, HealthCorp has experienced revenue erosion while peers are experiencing both top and bottom line growth. HealthCorp would like you to help diagnose the cause of this poor performance, and eventually, help formulate a course of action to improve revenue by $1B in the next two years.
prompt.question: Diagnose the cause of HealthCorp's revenue decline and recommend a course of action to improve revenue by $1B within two years.

clarifying_info.q: Does HealthCorp serve Medicare or Medicaid patients?
clarifying_info.a: HealthCorp does not have a material number of Medicare or Medicaid patients.

clarifying_info.q: What is happening in the provider market?
clarifying_info.a: The provider market with which HealthCorp works has undergone rapid consolidation within the last 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: Is there new competition in the market?
clarifying_info.a: HealthCorp has seen a large, for-profit disrupter enter the market in the last 2 years.

clarifying_info.q: How do health insurers set prices?
clarifying_info.a: Health insurers negotiate prices with physicians and hospital networks through system-by-system negotiations; prices are typically related to Medicare reimbursements.

clarifying_info.q: How much budget is available to fund improvement initiatives?
clarifying_info.a: HealthCorp is cash strapped and only has $10M to spend on initiatives.

exhibits.title: HealthCorp Revenue and NPS (2015-2017)
exhibits.shows: Two charts side by side: (1) HealthCorp annual revenue in $M for 2015, 2016, and 2017, and (2) HealthCorp Net Promoter Score (NPS) for the same three years.

exhibits.title: Portfolio of Internal Initiatives
exhibits.shows: A table listing seven potential internal projects, each with its cost, time to implement (in months), and projected NPS increase. NPS increase is realized only after project implementation.

framework: Revenue diagnosis: understand revenue drivers (premiums, enrollment, plan mix) and identify what is declining
Customer experience / NPS analysis: assess whether falling customer satisfaction is linked to revenue erosion
Competitive landscape: evaluate impact of new for-profit entrant and provider consolidation on pricing and membership
Initiative prioritization: evaluate a portfolio of NPS-improvement projects against cost, time, and NPS-efficiency constraints to hit $1B target within 2 years

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 1. What does the data tell you about HealthCorp's revenue trend and its relationship to NPS?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that revenue fell from $9,800M (2015) to $9,300M (2016) to $8,900M (2017) — a total decline of $900M. NPS fell from 16.0 to 13.5 to 11.5 over the same period. The candidate should identify a correlation: as NPS drops, revenue drops. They should then calculate revenue per NPS point to quantify the relationship and determine how many NPS points are needed to recover $1B.

math.setup: Revenue lost per NPS point drop: divide the year-over-year revenue change by the year-over-year NPS change for each period.
steps: To recover $1B in revenue: $1,000M / $200M per point = 5 NPS points needed
math.answer: Each NPS point is worth $200M in revenue. HealthCorp must improve NPS by at least 5 points to achieve the $1B revenue target.

questions.prompt: Given the need to raise NPS by 5 points within 2 years using at most $10M, which initiatives from Exhibit 2 should HealthCorp pursue?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply two constraints simultaneously: (1) total cost <= $10M, (2) implementation time <= 24 months (2-year deadline). They should calculate an NPS/cost efficiency index for each eligible project, rank by efficiency, and select the highest-efficiency combination that meets both constraints and delivers at least 5 NPS points. The optimal portfolio is: Develop mobile app + Partner with premier providers + Customer journey mapping.

math.setup: For each project within the 24-month deadline, compute NPS efficiency = NPS increase / cost ($M). Then select projects by descending efficiency until NPS >= 5 and total cost <= $10M.
steps: Compute efficiency index for remaining projects:
Implement rewards program: 4 NPS / $12M = 0.33 (rank 5; also exceeds $10M budget)
Select top 3 by efficiency: mobile app ($1.5M, +2 NPS) + premier providers ($3M, +2 NPS) + customer journey mapping ($4M, +2 NPS)
Expected revenue gain: 6 pts x $200M = $1,200M (exceeds $1B target)
math.answer: Pursue mobile app + partner with premier providers + customer journey mapping at a combined cost of $8.5M, delivering 6 NPS points and ~$1.2B in incremental revenue within 24 months.

brainstorming.prompt: Assuming HealthCorp's falling NPS is a key driver of revenue decline, what initiatives could HealthCorp undertake to increase its NPS?

categories.name: Digital / Technology
ideas: Develop a mobile app for claims tracking, ID cards, and provider search
Redesign the online member portal for easier navigation
Implement digital chat or AI-based customer support

categories.name: Claims & Operations
ideas: Redesign the claims process to reduce denial rates and speed up reimbursements

categories.name: Provider Network
ideas: Partner with premier / high-quality providers to improve care access
Expand the in-network provider list to reduce balance-billing surprises

categories.name: Customer Service
ideas: Outsource or restructure customer service to reduce wait times
Train call-center staff on empathy and first-call resolution
Offer dedicated care navigators for complex cases

categories.name: Community & Wellness
ideas: Invest in community health initiatives to build brand loyalty

categories.name: Rewards & Loyalty
ideas: Implement a rewards program for healthy behaviors
Offer premium discounts tied to engagement metrics

recommendation: HealthCorp should invest $8.5M in three initiatives — developing a mobile app (+2 NPS, 9 months), partnering with premier providers (+2 NPS, 16 months), and customer journey mapping (+2 NPS, 13 months) — to gain 6 NPS points and generate approximately $1.2B in incremental revenue, exceeding the $1B target within the 2-year window.
The CEO and CSO should simultaneously direct the corporate development team to explore M&A opportunities as a complementary growth lever.
risks: NPS-to-revenue relationship may not remain linear at higher NPS levels
Provider partnerships (16 months to implement) may face delays due to ongoing provider market consolidation
The for-profit competitor may continue to erode membership independent of NPS improvements
Realized NPS gains may be partially offset if the competitor continues to undercut on price
next_steps: Kick off mobile app development immediately (shortest timeline at 9 months)
Negotiate provider partnership agreements in parallel
Track NPS monthly to validate the $200M-per-point relationship and adjust portfolio if needed
Pursue M&A pipeline in parallel with internal initiatives
